nina: FYI - onboarding run for magnet13b-int4v2 (tidepool snapshot) surfaced a small but reproducible degradation on our long-context fidelity checks. quick dump below.

cheng: How small? and on which metric?

nina: Top-1 exact-match on the long-anchor QA set dropped from 0.781 -> 0.754 on the canary nodes (~3.5% absolute). This shows up only when the KV cache is resumed after a long prefill (>6k tokens). Short contexts unaffected.

leo: Interesting. Did the snapshot change RoPE scaling or prefill chunking?

nina: Two metadata diffs vs previous snap: `rope_gain` bumped from 1.0 -> 0.998 and `prefill_chunk_bytes` moved from 65536 -> 32768 (artifact of the prefill chunking refactor).

sam: Can you share the minimal repro? I can run on my dev GPU.

nina: Repro (use image rwinf/dev:stable-tidepool):
```
python eval/longqa.py --model magnet13b-int4v2 --snapshot s-2026-04-12-tidepool \
  --prompt tests/anchors/long-anchor-02.txt --max-tokens 8192 --kvcache-mode resume \
  --quant-kernel int4v2 --emit-json --seed 9
```
Baseline EM: 0.781, tidepool: 0.754. Diff ~0.027.

cheng: Does forcing `--rope-gain 1.0` or `--kvcache-chunk 65536` mitigate?

nina: Quick test: `--rope-gain 1.0` recovers to 0.779; `--kvcache-chunk 65536` -> 0.776; both together -> 0.780. So both knobs move the needle.

leo: So it's an interaction: smaller prefill chunks + slight rope_gain tweak. Could be accumulation rounding in int4v2 kernels when KV entries are stitched across chunk boundaries.

sam: I added a tiny probe that computes phase continuity across chunk boundaries. Running `tools/kv_phase_check --snapshot s-2026-04-12-tidepool` yields: 99.3% continuity within 1e-5, but a 0.7% cluster with deltas up to 3e-3 concentrated at chunk boundaries where tokens were split.

qa-bot: Queued longqa-regressions x5 with both snapshots for a full compare: https://ci.redwood-internal/longqa/1765439999

nina: I also compared logits deltas: LOGITS_SUMMARY {"chunk_boundary_bias": 0.0031, "phase_continuity_mean": 0.0009}. The bias correlates with rare tokens (low occ frequency) that get rounded differently depending on where their KV was written.

cheng: Two hypotheses: 1) prefill chunking causes partial writes where quantized accumulators see different rounding order; 2) rope_gain float truncation in snapshot metadata loses guard bits (we currently store as float16 to save space).

leo: Proposed short actions:
- run rehydrate-phase-scan across 10 snapshots (pre/post refactor) and collect delta histograms (nina/qa).
- change snapshot serialization for `rope_gain` to float32 and run a quick A/B. (eng)
- add unit that simulates chunk-split stitching across int4v2 kernel arithmetic and verify numeric parity (cheng).

sam: I'll start a kernel-level microbenchmark to replay accumulation orderings and measure variance. If ordering is the problem we could make chunk-stitch deterministic or add a small compensating correction on rehydrate.

ops-bot: Canary s-2026-04-12-tidepool deployed to 4% at 2026-04-12T14:40:10Z. Monitoring flagged longctx_em_drop=0.027.

qa-bot: Test run results (first 3): tidepool EM mean 0.755, baseline 0.782. Full runs queued.

nina: Given mitigations are cheap (store rope_gain float32 + revert to larger kvcache chunk size for snapshotting), I'm going to block further rollouts until ENG picks one. Adding this to the model-onboard checklist as a numeric parity gate.

leo: Agreed. I'm drafting a small patch to serialize selective metadata in float32 (rope_gain, phase_norm) and leave the rest compressed. PR incoming.

cheng: Also let's add an automated nightly that runs `tools/kv_phase_check` whenever a new snapshot is created and fails CI if tail > 1e-3 for long-prefill traces.

sam: Good call. That will catch these pre-RT regressions earlier.

nina: Thanks team. I'll attach the failing prompt and CI logs to the onboard ticket.
